note: Lenvatinib reached NSCLC patients on a filed H460 xenograft (monotherapy phase 2 directionally positive, OS p=0.065, never taken to phase 3), a RET-fusion cell model (16% ORR in RET-fusion patients) and a cross-indication CT26/BNL isograft rationale for the pembrolizumab combination that three LEAP phase 3s contradicted; two-species toxicology predicted the vascular harms, and famitinib and vorolanib have NSCLC patient data but no model comparison.
label: NSCLC (VEGFR multikinase)

engagement.confidence_note: Proxy opening date: Eisai study number M03012 (cf. M13012/M13013 = 2013 thyroid xenografts) implies 2003; the earliest public record is the 2015 FDA review, which lists the title only.
engagement.model: Human NSCLC cell-line xenografts in immunodeficient mice (H460 lenvatinib, A549 vorolanib)
engagement.note: Eisai's filed H460 lung xenograft read tumour volume; the published panel's PD readouts (tumour MVD, VEGFR2 phosphorylation) were never measured in NSCLC patients.
engagement.short: Xenograft MVD/pVEGFR2 never measured in patients
engagement.quote: M03012 E7080 Anti-tumor Effect in Human Lung Cancer H460 Xenograft Model in Mice
engagement.judgement: Study M03012 is listed by title only; Yamamoto 2014 (10.1186/2045-824x-6-18) gives the readouts (CD31 MVD, tumour pVEGFR2 in KP-1/VEGF). No NSCLC trial of a member drug reported a tumour MVD or receptor-phosphorylation series, so untested rather than a downstream same.

engagement.model: RET fusion-driven cells (CCDC6-RET lung and thyroid lines, Ba/F3-type assays) and RET-fusion NIH3T3 xenografts
engagement.note: Lenvatinib blocked KIF5B-RET, CCDC6-RET and NcoA4-RET autophosphorylation in cells; RET phosphorylation was never measured in dosed RET-fusion NSCLC patients.
engagement.short: RET autophosphorylation not measured in patients
engagement.quote: In cellular assays, lenvatinib inhibited auto-phosphorylation of KIF5B-RET, CCDC6-RET, and NcoA4-RET.
engagement.judgement: Abstract-level reading. Patient-level model (RET fusion selects responders). The Hida 2019 phase 2 took no on-treatment biopsies, so the direct readout has no human counterpart.

engagement.model: Syngeneic CT26 colon / BNL hepatoma mouse models of lenvatinib plus anti-PD-1 (immunocompetent BALB/c)
engagement.note: The combination rationale came from colon and hepatoma isografts (TAM depletion, CD8+ activation, type-I IFN signature); none of these were measured in LEAP NSCLC patients.
engagement.short: Immune PD readouts not measured in LEAP
engagement.quote: Flow cytometric analysis revealed that lenvatinib reduced tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) and increased the percentage of activated CD8+ T cells secreting interferon (IFN)-γ+ and granzyme B (GzmB).
engagement.judgement: Full text read (PMC6392299): models are CT26 colon, BNL hepatoma and B16-F10 melanoma; no lung model, hence cross_indication. LEAP-006/007/008 abstracts report no immune PD; a checker with full texts could revisit.
engagement.reason: No model PD readout measured in NSCLC patients

engagement.model: Syngeneic Lewis lung carcinoma (LLC) subcutaneous tumours in immunocompetent C57BL/6 mice: VEGFR TKI (famitinib 2022, lenvatinib 2026) added to radiotherapy plus PD-1/PD-L1 blockade
engagement.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC9715775). Published 2022-10-24 while the camrelizumab plus famitinib NSCLC cohorts (NCT04346381, primary completion 2022-06-22) were unreported and the paper cites no trial; no earlier conference disclosure found, so scored prospective, not retrodiction.
engagement.note: LLC tumours read CD8+ TIL, M1 TAM and MDSC by flow; no on-treatment immune readout exists from famitinib- or lenvatinib-treated NSCLC patients.
engagement.short: Mouse immune PD readouts never measured in patients
engagement.quote: Compared with radioimmunotherapy, the addition of famitinib further promoted the infiltration of CD8+ T cells and M1 type tumor associated macrophages, and reduced the number of myeloid suppressor cells.
engagement.judgement: One track for both LLC runs: same cell line (LLC), host (C57BL/6), RT schedule (3 x 8 Gy), checkpoint antibody dose (10 mg/kg) and prediction (a VEGFR TKI potentiates radio-immunotherapy); only the member drug differs. A lung-specific immunocompetent system, so distinct from the draft's cross-indication CT26/BNL isografts (syngeneic-ct26-bnl-mouse-lenvatinib-anti-pd1) and from the immunodeficient human xenograft track. Opening entry at first use; the model's PD readouts are tumour immune-cell counts that no NSCLC trial of a member drug has measured on treatment.
engagement.reason: Mouse immune readouts not measured in patients

dose.confidence_note: Proxy opening date: Eisai study number M03012 (cf. M13012/M13013 = 2013 thyroid xenografts) implies 2003; the earliest public record is the 2015 FDA review, which lists the title only.
dose.model: Human NSCLC cell-line xenografts in immunodeficient mice (H460 lenvatinib, A549 vorolanib)
dose.note: H460 xenograft dose range 3-100 mg/kg (Yamamoto 2014); neither the FDA review nor the paper states a mouse-to-human exposure match for lung.
dose.quote: M03012 E7080 Anti-tumor Effect in Human Lung Cancer H460 Xenograft Model in Mice
dose.judgement: The 2015 review's exposure margins are for toxicology species; Yamamoto 2014 gives doses only. The 24 mg NSCLC dose was the solid-tumour MTD from phase 1, not a model target, so the track stays untested even though Study 703 was directionally positive.
dose.reason: Model never stated an exposure target

dose.model: RET fusion-driven cells (CCDC6-RET lung and thyroid lines, Ba/F3-type assays) and RET-fusion NIH3T3 xenografts
dose.note: Cell-based RET-fusion model gives potencies, not an exposure target; Hida 2019 used the 24 mg solid-tumour dose with no model comparison.
dose.short: Cell potencies only; 24 mg from phase 1
dose.quote: Lenvatinib suppressed the growth of CCDC6-RET human thyroid and lung cancer cell lines, and as well, suppressed anchorage-independent growth and tumorigenicity of RET gene fusion-transformed NIH3T3 cells.
dose.judgement: Abstract-level reading; the NIH3T3 xenograft dose and any plasma exposure are in the full text, which I did not read. No source puts the RET-fusion cellular potency against clinical exposure, so untested.
dose.reason: No exposure target stated by the model

dose.model: Syngeneic CT26 colon / BNL hepatoma mouse models of lenvatinib plus anti-PD-1 (immunocompetent BALB/c)
dose.note: Mice got 3 or 10 mg/kg lenvatinib with anti-PD-1; no human exposure equivalent stated. LEAP later used 20 mg with pembrolizumab (phase 1b RP2D).
dose.quote: All animals received lenvatinib (3 or 10 mg/kg orally) once daily for the duration of time indicated by the black arrow in the figures.
dose.judgement: Full text read. The paper gives no mouse PK, so the 20 mg clinical dose (Study 111/KEYNOTE-146 RP2D, NCT02501096) cannot be called a reached model target on its own.

dose.model: Syngeneic Lewis lung carcinoma (LLC) subcutaneous tumours in immunocompetent C57BL/6 mice: VEGFR TKI (famitinib 2022, lenvatinib 2026) added to radiotherapy plus PD-1/PD-L1 blockade
dose.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC9715775). Published 2022-10-24 while the camrelizumab plus famitinib NSCLC cohorts (NCT04346381, primary completion 2022-06-22) were unreported and the paper cites no trial; no earlier conference disclosure found, so scored prospective, not retrodiction.
dose.note: Famitinib 5 mg/kg (lenvatinib 4 mg/kg in 2026) daily in mice; no human-equivalent exposure stated; patients got famitinib 20 mg once daily.
dose.quote: Famitinib (5 mg/kg, N685200402) was given daily by intragastric administration from days 1 to 14
dose.judgement: One track for both LLC runs: same cell line (LLC), host (C57BL/6), RT schedule (3 x 8 Gy), checkpoint antibody dose (10 mg/kg) and prediction (a VEGFR TKI potentiates radio-immunotherapy); only the member drug differs. A lung-specific immunocompetent system, so distinct from the draft's cross-indication CT26/BNL isografts (syngeneic-ct26-bnl-mouse-lenvatinib-anti-pd1) and from the immunodeficient human xenograft track. Neither LLC paper states a mouse-to-human exposure match, so, as the draft scores the H460 and RET tracks, there is nothing to compare with the 20 mg famitinib or 20 mg lenvatinib clinical doses: untested.

efficacy.confidence_note: Proxy opening date: Eisai study number M03012 (cf. M13012/M13013 = 2013 thyroid xenografts) implies 2003; the earliest public record is the 2015 FDA review, which lists the title only.
efficacy.model: Human NSCLC cell-line xenografts in immunodeficient mice (H460 lenvatinib, A549 vorolanib)
efficacy.note: Eisai filed an H460 lung xenograft (M03012); the review gives the title, not the result. No NSCLC trial yet.
efficacy.short: Filed H460 lung xenograft, result unpublished
efficacy.quote: M03012 E7080 Anti-tumor Effect in Human Lung Cancer H460 Xenograft Model in Mice
efficacy.judgement: Listed to date the model before Study 703 (NCT01529112, started Nov 2011). Yamamoto 2014 publishes the same cell line: H460 ΔTV 34.9% at 3 mg/kg to -0.8% at 100 mg/kg, significant from 3 mg/kg.

efficacy.model: RET fusion-driven cells (CCDC6-RET lung and thyroid lines, Ba/F3-type assays) and RET-fusion NIH3T3 xenografts
efficacy.note: Lenvatinib inhibited RET-fusion signalling and growth in CCDC6-RET lung cells and RET-fusion NIH3T3 tumours; a patient-selection prediction before any RET-fusion trial.
efficacy.quote: These results demonstrate that lenvatinib can exert antitumor activity against RET gene fusion-driven tumor models by inhibiting oncogenic RET gene fusion signaling.
efficacy.judgement: Abstract-level reading. Published July 2013, three months after NCT01877083 opened (April 2013), but before any patient result; prediction_level patient because the model names the responder genotype.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: xenograft growth inhibition versus OS/PFS direction in a placebo-controlled phase 2
efficacy.confidence_note: Quote is the registry's structured primary-outcome fields (medians in weeks with 95% CI), not a sentence. The hazard ratio and p-value come from the EU register results (2011-002347-10, first published 2019-01-19). The ASCO 2014 abstract (Havel et al., J Clin Oncol 32:15_suppl 8043, May 2014) was the first public report but could not be fetched (ascopubs 403), so the entry is dated to the ClinicalTrials.gov results posting.
efficacy.model: Human NSCLC cell-line xenografts in immunodeficient mice (H460 lenvatinib, A549 vorolanib)
efficacy.note: Study 703: lenvatinib 24 mg vs placebo, >=2 prior regimens; OS 38.4 vs 24.1 weeks (HR 0.70, p=0.065), PFS 20.9 vs 7.9 weeks.
efficacy.short: Phase 2 OS/PFS favoured lenvatinib; no phase 3
efficacy.quote: Overall Survival (OS) ... Lenvatinib 38.4 (26.57 to 47.86) ... Lenvatinib Matched Placebo 24.1 (15.29 to 36.43)
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me: model side Yamamoto 2014 (H460 growth inhibition, no regression), patient side the registry record (tier 3). Direction agrees on OS, PFS and ORR, but the primary OS analysis missed two-sided p<0.05 (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.45-1.03, p=0.065 on the EU register) and Eisai never ran a monotherapy phase 3, so a stricter reader could leave this unresolved. Not scored contra: nothing in the patient data points the other way. Vorolanib's A549 xenograft (Mol Ther Oncolytics 2022, 10.1016/j.omto.2022.01.001) joins this track, but its only NSCLC trial is a nivolumab combination (listed below) that the monotherapy xenograft did not predict, so it changes no status. Famitinib has NSCLC phase 2 data (listed) and three terminated phase 3s (NCT02766140, NCT04619433, NCT05106335) but no preclinical NSCLC model I could find (Europe PMC, abstract level).

patient_trials.quote: The objective response rate per cohort were as follows: NSCLC naive 33% (five of 15, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 13%-60%), NSCLC primary refractory 5.9% (one of 17, 95% CI: 0%-17.6%), NSCLC acquired resistance 11.1% (two of 18, 95% CI: 0%-27.8%);
For all patients, the confirmed ORR was 30.4%, and the disease control rate was 95.7%.
With a median follow-up of 18.1 months, the confirmed ORR was 42.9% (95% confidence interval [CI] 24.5-62.8).

efficacy.model: Syngeneic CT26 colon / BNL hepatoma mouse models of lenvatinib plus anti-PD-1 (immunocompetent BALB/c)
efficacy.note: Lenvatinib plus anti-PD-1 beat either agent alone in CT26 and BNL isografts; offered as the rationale for the pembrolizumab combination, no NSCLC trial yet.
efficacy.short: Combination beat single agents in isografts
efficacy.quote: Antitumor activity of lenvatinib plus anti-PD-1 was greater than that of either single treatment.
efficacy.judgement: Full text read. Opens the combination track at its first publication (Feb 2019), the month LEAP-006/007 were registered; the earlier Study 111 NSCLC cohort (ORR 33%) is patient data, not a model. Cross-indication because no lung model was used.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: growth inhibition of RET-fusion cells and tumours versus ORR/PFS in RET-fusion patients
efficacy.model: RET fusion-driven cells (CCDC6-RET lung and thyroid lines, Ba/F3-type assays) and RET-fusion NIH3T3 xenografts
efficacy.note: Phase 2 in 25 RET-fusion lung adenocarcinomas: ORR 16% (primary endpoint), DCR 76%, median PFS 7.3 months; activity as predicted, but weak.
efficacy.quote: Lenvatinib demonstrated activity in patients with RET fusion-positive lung adenocarcinomas; although the response rate was relatively low, the median PFS supports the activity of lenvatinib in these patients.
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me (model Okamoto 2013; the trial paper cites the model, which is a pairing, not a statement). Scored same at patient level with source_calls_it partial, my reading of the authors' own 'relatively low' wording: direction agreed, magnitude was modest and no registration followed. A stricter reader could score contra on the 16% primary ORR; I did not, because the model predicted activity, not a response-rate bar. Abstract-level reading; registry results posted 2019-08-13, before the paper.

patient_trials.quote: The overall ORR was 16% (95% CI: 4.5%-36.1%). At data cutoff (February 3, 2016), the median PFS was 7.3 months (95% CI: 3.6-10.2) and the median OS was not reached.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: model: combination superior to anti-PD-1 alone; patients: OS HR 1.10 for the addition of lenvatinib
efficacy.population: Unselected, PD-L1 TPS >=1%, first line (LEAP-007); nonsquamous first line (LEAP-006); post-ICI (LEAP-008)
efficacy.model: Syngeneic CT26 colon / BNL hepatoma mouse models of lenvatinib plus anti-PD-1 (immunocompetent BALB/c)
efficacy.note: LEAP-007: adding lenvatinib to first-line pembrolizumab gave OS HR 1.10 (futility met) and more grade 3-5 toxicity; LEAP-006 and LEAP-008 also failed.
efficacy.short: Three LEAP phase 3s failed; OS HR 1.10
efficacy.quote: Lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab did not have a favorable benefit‒risk profile versus placebo plus pembrolizumab.
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me: model side Kato 2019 (tier 1); none of the LEAP abstracts cites a model. Dated to the ClinicalTrials.gov results posting (2022-06-02), before the JTO paper (online 29 Dec 2023). The isografts predicted combination benefit over PD-1 blockade alone; LEAP-007 (n=623) showed none on OS and PFS HR 0.78 did not meet its threshold, LEAP-008 (OS HR 0.98 vs docetaxel) and LEAP-006 (OS HR 1.05 with chemotherapy) agreed. One contra entry with the other two trials as patient_trials; nothing has reversed it. Abstract-level reading of all three.

patient_trials.quote: median (95% confidence interval [CI]) OS was 14.1 (11.4‒19.0) months in the lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab group versus 16.4 (12.6‒20.6) months in the placebo plus pembrolizumab group (hazard ratio = 1.10 [95% CI: 0.87‒1.39], p = 0.79744 [futility criterion met]).

Lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab did not improve efficacy versus docetaxel in participants with stage IV NSCLC that progressed on anti‒programmed cell death protein 1 or anti-programmed cell death ligand 1 therapy and platinum-containing chemotherapy.
Adding lenvatinib to first-line pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy did not improve efficacy versus pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy in stage IV nonsquamous NSCLC without targetable genetic alterations.

efficacy.reason: Isograft combination benefit absent in three phase 3s

efficacy.model: Syngeneic Lewis lung carcinoma (LLC) subcutaneous tumours in immunocompetent C57BL/6 mice: VEGFR TKI (famitinib 2022, lenvatinib 2026) added to radiotherapy plus PD-1/PD-L1 blockade
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC9715775). Published 2022-10-24 while the camrelizumab plus famitinib NSCLC cohorts (NCT04346381, primary completion 2022-06-22) were unreported and the paper cites no trial; no earlier conference disclosure found, so scored prospective, not retrodiction.
efficacy.note: Famitinib added to RT plus anti-PD-1 beat RT plus anti-PD-1 in LLC tumours; the camrelizumab plus famitinib NSCLC cohorts were still unreported.
efficacy.short: Famitinib triple beat radio-immunotherapy in LLC
efficacy.quote: In a mouse model, the triple therapy of famitinib, radiotherapy and immunotherapy had the most dramatic antitumor activity.
efficacy.judgement: One track for both LLC runs: same cell line (LLC), host (C57BL/6), RT schedule (3 x 8 Gy), checkpoint antibody dose (10 mg/kg) and prediction (a VEGFR TKI potentiates radio-immunotherapy); only the member drug differs. A lung-specific immunocompetent system, so distinct from the draft's cross-indication CT26/BNL isografts (syngeneic-ct26-bnl-mouse-lenvatinib-anti-pd1) and from the immunodeficient human xenograft track. Opening entry; groups were control, RT, anti-PD-1, RT + famitinib, RT + anti-PD-1 and the triple (n = 5 each), so the prediction is an add-on effect of famitinib over radio-immunotherapy.

efficacy.model: Syngeneic Lewis lung carcinoma (LLC) subcutaneous tumours in immunocompetent C57BL/6 mice: VEGFR TKI (famitinib 2022, lenvatinib 2026) added to radiotherapy plus PD-1/PD-L1 blockade
efficacy.population: Unselected NSCLC: first-line PD-L1 TPS >=1% (n=41) and post chemo-immunotherapy (n=40) cohorts of NCT04346381
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of both cohort papers (open access, PMC10882294 and PMC11087418); NCT04346381 has no results posted, so registry_date is null. Pairing made here: neither paper cites the LLC model.
efficacy.note: Single-arm camrelizumab plus famitinib cohorts (ORR 53.7% first-line, 7.5% post chemo-IO) lack RT and a famitinib-free arm; randomized phase 3s terminated or unreported.
efficacy.short: Single-arm doublet cohorts; no add-on test
efficacy.quote: the combination regimen of camrelizumab and famitinib achieved an ORR of 53.7% (95% CI 37.4% to 69.3%) and a DCR of 92.7% (95% CI 80.1% to 98.5%).
efficacy.judgement: Untested, not same + partial: the model predicted that famitinib adds to radio-immunotherapy, and a single-arm doublet without RT or a famitinib-free comparator cannot test an add-on effect; the ORR shows the doublet is active, which the draft already credits to the xenograft track. The controlled tests never read out: NCT04619433 (camrelizumab + chemo +/- famitinib, phase 3) terminated by sponsor at n = 48, NCT05106335 (vs docetaxel) terminated at n = 1 for R&D strategy, NCT05042375 (vs pembrolizumab, n = 450) status unknown with no results (ClinicalTrials.gov, read 2026-11-05). If the checker accepts single-arm activity in the predicted direction as a comparison (as the draft does for Hida 2019), this becomes same with source_calls_it partial and magnitude direction_only.

patient_trials.quote: The median PFS was 16.6 months (95% CI 8.3 to not reached), and OS data were not yet mature, with an estimated 12-month OS rate of 76.8% (95% CI 60.0% to 87.3%).
The ORR and DCR with this combination regimen were 7.5% (95% CI, 1.6-20.4) and 80.0% (95% CI, 64.4-90.9), respectively.

efficacy.model: Syngeneic Lewis lung carcinoma (LLC) subcutaneous tumours in immunocompetent C57BL/6 mice: VEGFR TKI (famitinib 2022, lenvatinib 2026) added to radiotherapy plus PD-1/PD-L1 blockade
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC12773621): received 2025-08-14, accepted 2025-12-23, published 2026-01-02; groups control, RT, RT + anti-PD-L1, triple (n = 8); no lenvatinib + anti-PD-L1 arm without RT; LEAP-006/007/008 are not cited.
efficacy.note: Lenvatinib 4 mg/kg added to RT plus anti-PD-L1 extended LLC survival 29.5 to 34 days; no NSCLC trial of that triple exists.
efficacy.short: Post-LEAP lenvatinib triple in LLC; no trial
efficacy.quote: The triple-combination (RT + anti-PD-L1 + Lenvatinib) significantly suppressed tumor progression (P < 0.05) and extended median survival (34 vs. 29.5 days, P < 0.05) versus dual therapy.
efficacy.judgement: Not scored as a retrodiction (retrodiction false, status untested): the run post-dates the LEAP failures (LEAP-007 results 2022-06-02, LEAP-008 2024-08-22, LEAP-006 2025-02-21) but never ran the LEAP regimen (no lenvatinib + checkpoint arm without RT), does not cite LEAP, and predicts a triple (RT + anti-PD-L1 + lenvatinib) that no NSCLC trial has tested (ClinicalTrials.gov lenvatinib + radiotherapy in lung cancer: none, 2026-11-05). Under decision 10 it is a fresh prospective prediction awaiting its trial. If rule question 5 is settled the other way (any post-failure model of the lenvatinib + checkpoint pairing is a retrodiction), this entry becomes contra with retrodiction true, because the model did not reproduce the human null. Same track as the famitinib run (see track note).
efficacy.reason: Triple regimen never tested in NSCLC patients

safety.confidence_note: Quote is a verified fragment of the review sentence; proxy opening date.
safety.model: GLP repeat-dose toxicology in rat plus monkey (and dog)
safety.note: Lenvatinib's 4-week rat study was first reviewed under the IND in 2005; no patient comparison existed yet.
safety.quote: originally reviewed by Wei Chen, Ph.D. in April, 2005 following submission of IND
safety.judgement: One safety track pools the standard rodent plus non-rodent GLP toxicology (rat, monkey, dog for lenvatinib). Proxy opening date from the review's own history of the IND study. Famitinib and vorolanib toxicology was not retrievable (no NDA).

safety.magnitude_basis: haemorrhage from vascular lesions, animals vs patients
safety.model: GLP repeat-dose toxicology in rat plus monkey (and dog)
safety.note: Vascular lesions with haemorrhage in rat and monkey tissues predicted the haemorrhagic and arterial thromboembolic events, including fatal intracranial haemorrhage, seen in patients.
safety.quote: Consistent with nonclinical findings, hemorrhagic events including fatal intracranial hemorrhage have been observed in patients administered lenvatinib, as well as other VEGF antagonists.
safety.judgement: Comparison stated by the reviewer; imported from the thyroid-cancer NDA population (MONDO id as used by the sibling HCC draft, not re-verified by me). The review also pairs rat/monkey proteinuria with clinical proteinuria and vascular necrosis with hypertension/RPLS; the haemorrhage pairing is the one that matters most in lung cancer, where VEGF-pathway bleeding is the class worry.

safety.magnitude_basis: hypertension and proteinuria incidence, animals vs NSCLC patients
safety.model: GLP repeat-dose toxicology in rat plus monkey (and dog)
safety.note: In RET-fusion NSCLC patients the leading toxicities were hypertension (68%) and proteinuria (48%), the harms rat and monkey vascular and renal findings predicted.
safety.quote: The most common TEAEs were hypertension (68%), nausea (60%), decreased appetite (52%), diarrhea (52%), and proteinuria (48%).
safety.judgement: Paired by me: model side is the 2015 review (proteinuria in rats and monkeys 'consistent with clinical findings of proteinuria'; vascular necrosis 'suggestive of lenvatinib-mediated hypertension'). First in-disease confirmation, so strengthens. Nothing NSCLC-specific that animals missed could be found: LEAP-007 grade 3-5 TRAEs 57.9% vs 24.4% and LEAP-006 grade 5 5.6% vs 2.7% are class harms the review predicted; whether squamous-histology pulmonary haemorrhage occurred is not in the abstracts and a checker with LEAP-007 full text could test it. Abstract-level reading.
safety.reason: Class vascular harms matched in NSCLC patients
